messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: vector-valued constraints
parts:
Hi Folks -

Sorry if this has been posted before, but after doing some searching, I wasn't able to find it.

I'm implementing a model where a subset of individuals have a latent variable corresponding to an unobserved infection time. That time can only happen on the interval from birth to their current age, a_i. But individuals are of different ages, and I want to ensure that the value of the parameter is only between [0,a_i) for each individual. 

From the manual, it's doesn't seem like a vector-valued constraint will work in stan when declaring a vector of parameters.

One thought I had was to declare a vector of raw parameter values Z, constrained between [0,1) and then transform them by multiplying by Z * A elementwise where A = [a_1, a_2, ...a_N]. 

I know this would involve a jacobian adjustment, since I want to sample the values of Z*A. So, I wanted to see if I was missing something about using vector-valued constraints and check to see what the appropriate jacobian adjustment would be for the approach I described. 

Thanks!

-Jon

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] vector-valued constraints
parts:
If A is constant, you don't need a Jacobian adjustment.
If you work it out, it'll just add a log constant, so it
can be dropped because Stan only needs densities defined
up to an additive constant on the log scale.

- Bob
